full_judgment:
2. The petitioner is the printer and publisher of Bengali daily Ittefaq on behalf of Ittefaq Group of Publications. The petitioner is also the printer and publisher of English Weekly "New Nation" which had earlier received authentication from the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca through the Additional Deputy Commissioner, City, Dacca on 14.6.77 under section 12 of the Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973. 

 4. So far as the Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973 is concerned, sections 5, 7 and 12 thereof are relevant for the purpose of disposal of this Rule. Section 5 of the Act says that no newspaper shall be printed or published except in conformity with the provisions of this part of the Act and unless there subsists an authenticated declaration in respect thereof. Section 7 of the Act says that the printer and publisher of every newspaper shall appear in person or by agent authorised on his behalf in accordance with the rules, before the District Magistrate within whose local jurisdiction such newspaper shall be printed and published, and shall make and subscribe a declaration in Form-B of the schedule to the Act. Section 12 of the Act lays down the procedure for the authentication of a declaration in respect of a newspaper. Sub-section 1 of section 12 of the Act says that the authentication shall be made by the signature and official seal of the District Magistrate before whom the declaration is made. Sub-section 2 of section 12 of the Act says that the District Magistrate shall not authenticate the declaration unless he is satisfied upon certain require rents referred to in clauses a-h thereof. Sub-section 3 of section 12 of the Act says that if the District Magistrate refuses to authenticate the declaration, the person making the declaration may prefer an appeal to the Government against such refusal within 45 days. Sub-section 4 of section 12 of the Act says that if the District Magistrate falls to authenticate the declaration within 60 days of the making thereof, the person making the declaration may prefer an application to the Government praying for an order directing the District Magistrate to authenticate the declaration. 

 5. From a consideration of sections 7 and 12 along with its sub-sections under clauses there-under of the Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973 it clearly appears that the power to authenticate a declaration has been given to the District Magistrate within whose jurisdiction a particular newspaper Is to be printed and published and that against any refusal or inability of the District Magistrate to authenticate any declaration, an appeal shall lie to the Government. So far as the District Magistrate is concerned it has not been defined anywhere in the Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973 and consequently the only description thereof made in section 10 of the Code of Criminal Procedure will have to be followed In the present scheme of the executive and judicial administration of the Government although the same person combine the office of the Deputy Commissioner and District Magistrate the office of the District Magistrate Is quite separate and distinct from the office of the Deputy Commissioner, it is a creature of a statute by dint of section 10 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and such office is primarily a quasi judicial if not a judicial office as such. Thus it would clearly appear that any reference made in any statute to District Magistrate for making a decision, such proceeding by its very nature becomes a quasi judicial one. In Printing Press and Publication (Declarative and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973 the power to authenticate a declaration being given to the District Magistrate such proceeding by its nature becomes a quasi judicial one the provision of sections 7 & 12 of the Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973 speak for itself that such proceeding is a quasi judicial one. Section 7 says that the printer and publisher of every newspaper shall appear either in person of through agent before the District Magistrate while making and subscribing a declaration. Sub-section (2) of section 12 empowers the District Magistrate to authenticate a declaration after being satisfied about the requirements contained in clauses a-h therein. Sub-section (3) of section 12 further provides for a statutory appeal to the Government against any decision of the District Magistrate refusing to authenticate a declaration. Considering the aforesaid provisions of sections 7 and 12 of the Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973, there cannot remain any doubt that the proceeding before the District Magistrate as aforesaid in a quasi judicial one which warrants the District Magistrate to afford a personal hearing to the person making the declaration to satisfy the District Magistrate as to whether such person did fulfil the requirements contained in clauses a-h of sub-section 2 of section 12 of the Act as aforesaid. In this connection it may be mentioned that the language of sub-section (2) of section 12 of Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973 is negative in nature i.e. the District Magistrate shall not authenticate the declaration unless he is satisfied that the person concerned did fulfil the requirements contained in clauses a-h thereof This inevitably means that if a person making a declaration can satisfy the District Magistrate that the requirements contained in clauses a-h of sub-section (2) of section 12 of the Act have been fulfilled, in such circumstances the District Magistrate has no other option but to authenticate the declaration as such. 

 6. In the present case it will have to be considered whether the District Magistrate as aforesaid was satisfied as to whether the petitioner fulfilled the requirements of clauses a-h of sub-section 2 of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973. Although notice of this Rule was served upon the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca being the respondents herein and although the order of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca has been impugned in this Rule, a Section Officer in the Ministry of Home Affairs has only affirmed and filed an affidavit-in-opposition to this Writ petition and no affidavit-in-opposition has been filed on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca as such. Consequently, this Court had to call for the relevant filo or this case lying with the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca and it was produced before the Court by she learned Additional Attorney General appearing for the respondent concerned. From the perusal of the file, the notice of the court was drawn to memo No. 1090 (Eng)/Gen/X/1/78 dated 6.10.78 addressed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Gen) Dacca to the Section Officer, Ministry of Home Affairs. In such memo it has been stated that as the declaration of weekly "New Nation" given by the same petitioner was earlier authenticated with the concurrence of the Home Ministry this met/ also be decided by the Government accordingly. It appear from the file that in memo No. 7291/62/77 General dated 12.7.18 addressed from office of the Deputy Inspector General of Police, Special Branch similar view has been taken. From the foregoing facts and circumstances of the case it would clearly appear that the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca acting as the District Magistrate of Dacca had nothing to say that the petitioner did not fulfill the requirements of clauses of sub-section (2) of section 12 of Act XXII of 1973 and the satisfaction of the authority in question is evident from reference to the fact that the petitioner's earlier declaration as a printer and publisher of weekly “New Nation” was already authenticated by the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca upon concurrence from the Home Ministry. So far as the fulfilment of requirements under clauses a-h of sub-section (2) of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973 is concerned it has not made any difference between a weekly newspaper and a daily newspaper In the present case when the petitioner's declaration with regard to the weekly "New Nation" was already earlier authenticated by the District Magistrate of Dacca being satisfied that she petitioner had fulfilled the requirements of clauses a-h of sub-section 2 of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973, such authentication for a declaration of daily "'New Nation" could not be withheld by the said District Magistrate on the around that the petitioner did not fulfil the requirement of clauses a-h of sub-section 2 of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973, In such circumstances, as in the earlier authentication of the declaration wish regard to the weekly New Nation" was done with the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Deputy Commissioner referred the matter to the Ministry of Home Affairs for final decision with regard to the authentication of the declaration of the daily "New Nation". 

 7. In the foregoing facts and circumstances, when it is absolutely clear that the petitioner had fulfilled the requirements of clauses a-h of sub-section (2) of section 12 of acts XXIII of 1973, the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca acting as a District Magistrate was obliged under all circumstances to authenticate the petitioner's declaration with regard to the printing and publication of the daily New Nation" and the Deputy Commissioner in such circumstances could not refer the matter to the Ministry of Home Affairs of the Government of Bangladesh since a statutory appeal lies with the Government horn any decision of the District Magistrate refusing to authenticate a declaration. The impugned memo of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca suffers from a patent illegality in refusing to authenticate the declaration of the petitioner for printing and publishing of daily 'New Nation" when the same authority was satisfied that the petitioner did fulfill all the requirements of sub-section (2 of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973. In view of the earlier authentication of the petitioner's declaration with regard to weekly 'New Nation" with the concurrence of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca acting as a District Magistrate further acted illegally in referring the matter to the Ministry of 14 time Affairs when under sub-section (3) of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973, the Government is the statutory appellate authority against any refusal of District Magistrate to authenticate a declaration By such action, not only that the petitioner has been deprived from preferring an appeal to the Government, but the Deputy Commissioner acting as the District Magistrate refused to authenticate the declaration of the petitioner upon an instruction from its appellate authority. The impugned memo of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca also suffered from non compliance of the principle and rule of natural justice when the petitioner was never accorded any hearing of this matter when a proceeding before a District Magistrate under Sections 7 and 12 of Act XXIII of 1973 has been held to be quasi judicial in nature.
